setting: home and school reflections about time; memories and imagined time visibly separated from present reality

sentences.english: One afternoon, I suddenly felt, “Time is really something strange.”
sentences.japanese: ある午後、ふと「時間って、ほんとにふしぎだな」と感じました。

sentences.english: When I looked at the clock, it was just past noon.
sentences.japanese: 時計を見ると、ちょうど正午を過ぎたところ。

sentences.english: Only one minute ago, I was cleaning up after lunch.
sentences.japanese: たった1分前に、お昼ご飯のあと片付けをしていたばかり。

sentences.english: Yet already, I was thinking about the hours until dinner.
sentences.japanese: それなのに、もう夕ご飯までの時間のことを考えている自分がいました。

sentences.english: “In half an hour, my favorite anime will start,” my sister said, staring at the clock.
sentences.japanese: 「あと30分で好きなアニメが始まる」と、妹は時計をじっと見つめて言いました。

sentences.english: My father pointed at an old photograph.
sentences.japanese: 父は、わたしが小さかったころの姿を見せてくれました。

sentences.english: “A century ago, people did not have such accurate clocks.”
sentences.japanese: 「時間はみんなを少しずつ変えていくんだよ」と父は言いました。

sentences.english: When I think about the time of the past, I feel a little strange.
sentences.japanese: 時間って不思議だとわたしは思いました。

sentences.english: There are still many hours until midnight.
sentences.japanese: 夜中までにはまだたくさんの時間があります。

sentences.english: But second by second, the time moves forward into the future.
sentences.japanese: でも、一秒ずつ、時間は未来へと進んでいくのです。

sentences.english: A quarter of the day is morning, another quarter is before noon, another is afternoon, and the last quarter is night.
sentences.japanese: 一日の4分の1は朝、次の4分の1は午前、その次が午後、最後の4分の1が夜。

sentences.english: When I think of it that way, the flow of a day feels well balanced.
sentences.japanese: そんなふうに考えると、一日の流れが、きれいにバランスのとれたものに感じられます。
ご覧いただき、ありがとうございました。
